assets.scope: briagh-lair, sandworm-lair, eruan (vermin/sandworm, non-unique, explicit nice_tile tall body); the scripted sandworm burrower/huge burrower and the gigantic corrosive tunneler / gravity worm are other names and stay native or already-mapped as before

references.note: Approved disc, lighting and camera; do not copy its creature.

Native shape (64x128 tall): a thick tan-brown segmented worm rearing straight up from a crater of earth, its top split open into a four-petal flower-like maw lined in red-brown flesh, with crackling blue lightning arcing around it.
Shipped sandworm destroyer (closed rust-orange ring with a toothy round mouth): the tunneler is a thicker earth-brown worm reared up with a four-petal split maw, not a coiled ring.

prompt_fields.subject: A gigantic thick tunneling sandworm rearing up from the middle of the disc, drawn compact and smaller: a very thick segmented earth-brown and dusty umber body with fine ring ridges and paler tan underbelly bands coiling once around its own base in a low small heap of broken stone chunks kept close against the body, the front third reared up toward the viewer with its head split open into a wide four-petalled flower-like maw, each petal short and lined inside with glossy red-brown flesh and a few blunt pale teeth, a dark throat at the centre. Everything stays tightly clustered in the middle of the disc. No lightning, no glow.
prompt_fields.contrast: Sandworm tokens: sandworm (slim orange S-curve), sandworm destroyer (closed rust-orange ring with a round toothy mouth), sandworm burrower (green arches on a sand heap), sandworm queen. The tunneler is the only thick earth-brown worm reared up with a four-petal split maw over a rubble heap (silhouette: thick coil plus reared petal head; hue: umber earth brown, not orange, not green; value: mid).
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Disc plate discipline: measured results show generations of this style reference tend to render the disc DARKER than the reference, never lighter. So do not darken the disc at all: render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band and the area under the creature -- at the style reference's own brightness, if anything a hair lighter, and never darker. No warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette anywhere on the disc. Do not darken the creature to compensate either. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. Calibration from the previous generation of this exact token: it drew parts of the creature (the four petals and the rubble heap) past the edge of the disc, so the token could not be exported. This time draw the creature markedly smaller and tighter: the ENTIRE figure, including every petal, horn, droplet, spray and rubble chunk, fits inside a circle of about two thirds of the disc radius around the disc centre, leaving a wide bare charcoal ring of base plate on every side.
prompt_fields.palette: Mid earth-brown and dusty umber body lifted with paler tan segment bands and lighter ridge highlights, glossy red-brown maw interior, pale blunt teeth, light grey-tan stone chunks; nothing darker than mid tone except the throat. Dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept a visibly lighter value than the creature's darkest parts so the two never merge.
